solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Redeployed invader not new or changed

indicators.note: redeployed troops are moved into new positions, so the letters are arranged afresh
not says the letter for new is left out

explanation.surface: An invading force moved to a fresh position, its orders altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not new' removes N from INVADER, and 'Redeployed' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something varied has been altered or modified, so the past participle matches.

clue.text: Stages final parts of double weddings

indicators.note: final parts of says keep only the closing pair of letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A couple's double wedding unfolds in stages, now at the final part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final parts of' keeps the last two letters of each word: LE from 'double' and GS from 'weddings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stages of a journey or competition are its separate sections, the parts run one after another.

clue.text: There's hope when greedy-guts has to hand over a grand for a share

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: has to hand over says the greedy one gives up the grand

parts.note: a pig is a greedy eater
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Hope remains when a glutton must pay out a thousand for a stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is only padding between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a hope or ambition, something longed for.

clue.text: Takeaway food setter gets by going up in silence

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the silencing word

parts.note: to gag is to silence

indicators.note: going up in a down entry reads the word backwards

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler quietly sneaks off with a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the compiler but is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A doggy bag carries home a restaurant's leftovers, the food you take away from the meal.

clue.text: Woman's short description of ringer

parts.note: to describe something you say what it is a type of, so this supplies 'is a'

indicators.note: short says the last letter of the ringer is cut off

parts.note: a bell is a ringer

explanation.surface: A woman's brief summary of a bell-ringer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's' is the definition with 's standing for is; dropping the last L from IS A BELL leaves the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a girl's name, the Spanish form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Shark almost crazy by the end of the fight

indicators.note: almost says leave off the last letter

parts.note: mad means crazy
KO is a knockout, which ends a boxing match

explanation.surface: A shark goes nearly berserk as the fight finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The mako is a fast species of shark found in warm seas.

clue.text: Metal group's press people accepting help

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: accepting says the word for people takes in the help

parts.note: men means people
aid means help

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal band's PR people take on assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the media but is the verb to iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Maiden are a long-running British heavy metal band.

clue.text: What's germane about the Middle East

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean region

explanation.surface: A question of what is pertinent to the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means pertinent, a close synonym for bearing on the matter in hand.

clue.text: Dislikes adult interpretations

definitions.note: plural noun here, matching the plural answer

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
versions are particular renderings or readings of something

explanation.surface: Someone objects to grown-up readings of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversions are strong feelings of dislike, so the plural noun matches the plural dislikes.

clue.text: Strangely eager to contract

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the next word are to be arranged oddly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is oddly keen to sign a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges EAGER. 'Contract' is the verb, as in to contract to do a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to make a binding arrangement, which means coming to terms with another party.

clue.text: Some captains win games with such bowling

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cricket remark that some skippers win matches thanks to a particular kind of delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'with', which is only the link joining wordplay to definition; 'such bowling' alone stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a ball that curves in the air towards the batsman is a type of swing delivery, the kind meant here.

clue.text: Chocolate cake to have covered in cheese

indicators.note: covered in says the word for having sits wrapped inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A recipe suggestion: eat your chocolate cake smothered in cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense, fudgy square of chocolate sponge is the classic American bake of that name.

clue.text: Country house lawyer comes to tea

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
cha (or char) is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: A lawyer pops round to a country house for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian second home in the countryside, a type of rural villa.

clue.text: 100 bones broken — these might be useful notes

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
ribs are bones

indicators.note: broken says the letters of these are smashed into another order

explanation.surface: After a hundred bones are broken, written notes come in handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crib sheets are crafty jottings of answers brought into an exam, notes that help.

clue.text: You wouldn't keep a cool head in this battle

definitions.text: You wouldn't keep a cool head in this
definitions.meaning: a woollen hood covering the head and face keeps it warm, so not cool
the 1854 Crimean War engagement famous for the Charge of the Light Brigade

explanation.surface: A warning that in this fight nobody stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep a cool head' reads as staying calm under fire; really it means your head would not stay cold inside a knitted hood.
explanation.definitionFit: The knitted face-covering helmet took its name from the Crimean battle, where soldiers wore them against the cold.

clue.text: Thinking about going at it another way

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: another way says the letters of the phrase are done differently, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone considers tackling a task differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives C, as circa, before the rearranged GOING AT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogitating is deep thinking, pondering a matter carefully.

clue.text: Drama working in a restaurant having omitted to take a lot of drugs

parts.note: a waiter or waitress is waiting at tables

indicators.note: to take says the word for omitted takes in, or holds, the drugs abbreviation

parts.note: to have forgot (forgotten) something is to have omitted it
OD is an overdose, too much of a drug

explanation.surface: A restaurant worker skipped taking a huge quantity of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgot' as a past participle is the older or American form of forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's play about two tramps waiting for someone who never arrives is a famous stage work.

clue.text: Openings for actor really hoping to get into poorer film

indicators.note: to get into says those initials go inside the word for poorer

parts.note: worse means poorer in quality

indicators.note: openings for says take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An actor hopes to land a part in a lesser movie.
explanation.definitionFit: War Horse is Steven Spielberg's 2011 movie, from the novel and play.

clue.text: Musical show involving a treetop

indicators.note: involving suggests the letters are tangled up together, rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage musical with a treetop in the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light opera, a short musical stage work with spoken dialogue.

clue.text: Was Archishop of Canterbury internally backing organ's sound quality?

indicators.note: internally says the turned organ goes inside the archbishop's phrase

parts.note: the archbishop ran (headed) the CE, the Church of England

indicators.note: backing says the organ's word is read backwards

parts.note: the nose is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A question about whether a former archbishop backed the church organ's tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archishop' is the clue's own misspelling. The question mark flags the playful 'ran CE' reading of a former archbishop's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is the richness or depth of a tone, a characteristic of how something rings out.

clue.text: Somehow certain I should leave the drink

indicators.note: somehow says the letters left are arranged in some new way
should leave says the letter I is taken out of the word

explanation.surface: Someone sure they should walk away from alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should leave' drops I from CERTAIN; 'Somehow' rearranges CERTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth, nectar was the drink of the gods, so 'the drink' singles it out.

clue.text: After tea, we hear cricket side are left with varying pitch

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the drink
we hear says the drink's name is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the drink's name is said the same as the letter T
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: After the tea interval, a cricket team is left batting on a pitch of uneven bounce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' plays on the cricket ground but means musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal describes music built on keys and tones, so its pitches vary in a structured way.

clue.text: The end of April is good in French city

indicators.note: the end of says take the last letter of the next word

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: Late April is a fine time in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' wants to be the definition; 'French' belongs to 'good in French' and only 'city' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal.

clue.text: Touched, auntie regularly beginning to cry — with this sort of result?

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter, starting from the second of the first word
beginning to says take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An emotional aunt starts to weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' runs across both words: the even letters of 'Touched auntie' give OCEANI.
explanation.definitionFit: The tearful aunt's weeping produces an ocean of tears: a vast, sea-like outcome.

clue.text: Gun emplacement catches squadron leader in trap

indicators.note: in says that letter is put inside the trap

parts.note: a net is a trap

indicators.note: leader says take the first letter of squadron

explanation.surface: A gun position snares an air-force commander in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine-gun nest is a sheltered gun position, the military sense of the word.

clue.text: Puts underground storage unit in stone setting

indicators.note: in says the storage unit sits inside the rearranged stone
setting suggests the word stone is put into a new arrangement

parts.note: MB is a megabyte, a unit of computer storage

explanation.surface: Someone buries a storage unit, set in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts underground' suggests planting or mining, but it means burial. 'setting' rearranges the stone word around the storage unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb someone is to lay them in a grave or vault, burying the body.

clue.text: Some cream is only paste

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little cream is just a spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is a Japanese fermented soybean paste used in soups and sauces.

clue.text: Says missing the first tee is enough

indicators.note: missing the first says the first of two such letters is dropped

parts.note: states means says, declares
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T

explanation.surface: Someone declares that, without the opening tee shot, enough is enough.
explanation.walkthrough: STATES has two Ts; 'missing the first' drops only the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to fill to capacity, so food that sates is enough to satisfy hunger.

clue.text: Serves exactly 2200 scattered dots

parts.note: on the 24-hour clock 2200 is ten at night, so exactly then is at ten

indicators.note: scattered says the letters of dots are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: At ten at night, some dots get strewn about.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve customers is to look after their needs, a phrasal-verb synonym.
